sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, enforced by the compiler.
sketches.resonance: Loneliness isn't a feeling but a structural guarantee: the language itself ensures there will never be another.

sketches.mechanism: Optional chaining with `?.` silently returns nil and stops evaluation when any link in the chain is absent, collapsing the entire expression to nothing.
sketches.resonance: One absence anywhere in a lineage erases everything that would have followed — grief propagates backward through generations.

sketches.mechanism: In Erlang, a variable can only be bound once; rebinding the same variable is a match error, not an assignment.
sketches.resonance: In this language, you cannot overwrite what someone meant to you — the first binding is permanent, and any attempt to replace it crashes.
